        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">01 / GENERATIVE AI</span>

        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>Responsible GenAI, from architecture to evaluation</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">I design and teach applied generative and agentic AI systems that connect retrieval, orchestration, local model deployment, and monitoring—without losing sight of privacy or failure modes.</p>
          <p>The work spans RAG pipelines, multi-step agentic workflows, local models with Ollama, LangChain orchestration, and LangSmith-based tracing. In parallel, I have helped shape a privacy-preserving synthetic transaction-data project using Gaussian mixture models and differentially private variants, balancing utility with client privacy.</p>
          <div class="case-facts">
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Architecture</strong><span>Retrieval, orchestration, local inference, and observability</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Evaluation</strong><span>Baselines, trace inspection, error analysis, and fit-for-use criteria</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Guardrails</strong><span>Privacy, provenance, leakage, and human review</span></div>
          </div>
          <a class="inline-link" href="teaching.html">See the teaching practice →</a>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="case-study" id="genomic-ml" data-reveal>
        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">02 / COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY</span>
          <div class="case-tags"><span class="tag">Interpretable ML</span><span class="tag">Genomics</span><span class="tag">SHAP</span><span class="tag">Validation</span></div>
        </div>
        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>Reading the “genetic neighborhoods” of a poultry pathogen</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">Co-authored research tested whether genomic-island cassette organization could distinguish pathogenic from commensal <em>Enterococcus cecorum</em> lineages.</p>
          <p>The study encoded biologically meaningful cassette architecture across 145 genomes and used locked, genome-grouped cross-validation to reduce leakage risk. The resulting representation outperformed simpler genomic-island burden baselines, while cross-project validation made the remaining deployment limits explicit.</p>
          <div class="case-facts">
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>145 genomes</strong><span>95 commensal and 50 pathogenic isolates</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>0.918 AUROC</strong><span>Mean grouped cross-validation result for cassette-summary RF</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Honest limits</strong><span>Prospective validation required before operational deployment</span></div>
          </div>
          <a class="inline-link" href="https://doi.org/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1882753">Read the Frontiers paper →</a>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="case-study" id="open-source" data-reveal>
        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">03 / OPEN SOURCE</span>
          <div class="case-tags"><span class="tag">R</span><span class="tag">CRAN</span><span class="tag">Neural networks</span><span class="tag">Testing</span></div>
        </div>
        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>nnR: making neural-network algebra executable</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">A CRAN package that turns mathematical constructions on neural networks into inspectable R operations and pedagogical examples.</p>
          <p>nnR implements algebraic operations on neural networks and their approximations, connecting theoretical work on neural-network polynomials to code. The package includes documentation, a vignette, and test coverage designed to make abstract constructions easier to study and reproduce.</p>
          <div class="case-facts">
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>CRAN 0.1.0</strong><span>Published package with binaries and reference manual</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Pedagogical</strong><span>Designed as an understandable proof of concept</span></div>
            <div class="case-fact"><strong>Research-linked</strong><span>Grounded in peer-reviewed and preprint literature</span></div>
          </div>
          <a class="inline-link" href="https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=nnR">Open nnR on CRAN →</a>
          <br>
          <a class="inline-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01058">Read the mathematical framework →</a>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="case-study" data-reveal>
        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">04 / SYSTEMS</span>
          <div class="case-tags"><span class="tag">Rust</span><span class="tag">Bioinformatics</span><span class="tag">Quality control</span></div>
        </div>
        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>RustQC: exploring leaner genomic quality control</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">An experimental Rust implementation of core sequencing quality-control ideas, built to explore portability, performance, and clearer deployment.</p>
          <p>The project reworks parts of the familiar FastQC workflow in Rust and generates inspectable reports. It reflects a broader interest in pairing scientific correctness with systems-level efficiency.</p>
          <a class="inline-link" href="https://github.com/2shakilrafi/rustqc">View the repository →</a>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="case-study" data-reveal>
        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">05 / HEALTH ANALYTICS</span>
          <div class="case-tags"><span class="tag">Causal inference</span><span class="tag">Time series</span><span class="tag">Shiny</span></div>
        </div>
        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>From healthcare claims to decision-ready evidence</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">Applied causal, regression, Markov, and time-series methods to maternal-health and claims-volume questions in a health-insurance setting.</p>
          <p>The work integrated claims with built-environment, social determinants, socioeconomic, Census, and commercial data. Reproducible analyses and R Shiny dashboards helped translate technical output into usable evidence for stakeholders.</p>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="case-study" data-reveal>
        <div class="case-meta">
          <span class="case-number">06 / MEASUREMENT</span>
          <div class="case-tags"><span class="tag">Survey methods</span><span class="tag">Psychometrics</span><span class="tag">Product research</span></div>
        </div>
        <div class="case-body">
          <h2>Measurement frameworks for people-centered products</h2>
          <p class="case-deck">Designed and applied statistical analyses for behavioral-product evaluation and children’s nutritional-needs research.</p>
          <p>Projects included intervention comparisons using psychometric outcomes and complex-survey analysis using factor and structural models. The goal in each case was not just a result, but a defensible bridge from evidence to product or public-health decisions.</p>
        </div>
      </article>
